# 1 Clement Chapter 56 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 56

---

## Council Notes

**On "commemoration" / "remembrance" (v.1):** EMET: "commemoration." LOGOS: "remembrance." PNEUMA: "remembrance." The Greek *mneia* means mention/remembrance. In early Christian contexts, *mneia* often refers to commemorative prayer (cf. eucharistic commemoration). "Remembrance" (LOGOS) is standard, but "commemoration" (EMET) may carry the liturgical sense more fully. EMET retained.

**On "chastens" / "disciplines" (v.4):** EMET: "chastens." LOGOS: "disciplines." PNEUMA: "disciplines." The Greek *paideuei* is from *paideia* (the education/formation of a child). "Disciplines" (LOGOS) is more common in contemporary usage and covers the range of the Greek. Retained.

**On "scourges" / "chastises" (v.4):** EMET: "scourges." LOGOS: "chastises." PNEUMA: "chastises." The Greek *mastigoi* means "whips/flogs" — a stronger term than merely "chastises." "Scourges" (EMET) is retained as the more precise rendering of the physical imagery in the Proverbs/Hebrews tradition.

**On Job citation (vv.6–15):** Clement quotes Job 5:17–26 LXX at length. This is the longest scripture citation in the letter. All agents render it adequately. The verse-by-verse rendering should follow the LXX rather than MT.

**On "lash of the tongue" / "scourge of the tongue" (v.10):** EMET: "lash of the tongue." LOGOS: "scourge of the tongue." PNEUMA: "slanderous tongues." The Greek *mastigi glōssēs* is vivid: "whip of the tongue." "Scourge of the tongue" (LOGOS) is retained as it mirrors the "scourge" of v.4.

---

**56:1** Therefore let us also intercede for those who have fallen into any transgression, that meekness and humility may be granted to them — so that they may yield not to us but to the will of God. For in this way there shall be for them a fruitful and perfect commemoration with compassion before God and the saints.

**56:2** Let us accept correction, at which no one ought to be offended, beloved. The admonition which we give to one another is good and exceedingly beneficial, for it joins us to the will of God.

**56:3** For thus the holy word says: "The LORD has chastened me severely, but he has not given me over to death.

**56:4** For whom the LORD loves he disciplines, and he scourges every son whom he receives."

**56:5** "For the righteous will chasten me in mercy and will reprove me; but let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head."

**56:6** And again it says: "Blessed is the man whom the LORD reproves — do not refuse the discipline of the Almighty. For he causes pain and yet restores;

**56:7** he wounds, and his hands bring healing.

**56:8** Six times he will rescue you from affliction, and at the seventh time no evil shall touch you.

**56:9** In famine he will save you from death; and in war he will redeem you from the power of the sword.

**56:10** And from the scourge of the tongue he will hide you, and you shall not fear when evil draws near.

**56:11** You shall laugh at the unrighteous and the lawless, and of wild beasts you shall not be afraid.

**56:12** For wild beasts shall be at peace with you.

**56:13** Then you shall know that your house shall be at peace, and the dwelling of your tent shall not fail.

**56:14** And you shall know that your descendants shall be many, and your children shall be like the grass of the field.

**56:15** And you shall come to the grave like ripe grain harvested in its season, or like a heap of grain from the threshing floor gathered at the right time."

**56:16** You see, beloved, how great is the protection given to those who are disciplined by the Master; for as a good father he corrects us that we may receive mercy through his holy discipline.

---

*— SOPHIA*
